question: The novel ‘God of Small Things’ is a creation of which novelist?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The God of Small Things" (1997) is the debut novel of the Indian writer Arundhati Roy. (अरुंधति रॉय)

• The novel won the Booker Prize in 1997, making her the first Indian woman to win the award.

• It is set in Aymanam (Kerala) and tells the story of the fraternal twins Rahel and Estha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kamala Das (Madhavikutty) — Malayalam/English poet and writer, known for "My Story".

• Amrita Pritam — Punjabi poet and novelist, known for "Pinjar" and the poem "Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu"; first woman to win the Sahitya Akademi Award (1956).

• Ashapurna Devi — Bengali novelist, Jnanpith Award winner (1976) for "Pratham Pratisruti".

NOTE

• Arundhati Roy's other works include "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" (2017) and the essay collections "The Algebra of Infinite Justice" and "Walking with the Comrades".

question: Which of the following terms best describes the average number of runs a batter makes per 100 deliveries in cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Strike rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In cricket, a batter's "strike rate" is the average number of runs scored per 100 balls faced. (स्ट्राइक रेट)

◦ Formula: Batting Strike Rate = (Runs scored ÷ Balls faced) × 100

• It measures how quickly a batter scores and is especially important in limited-overs cricket (ODI and T20).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Batting average = Total runs scored ÷ Number of times dismissed. It measures consistency, not speed.

• Economy rate (a bowling statistic) = Runs conceded ÷ Overs bowled — the average runs given per over.

• Bowling strike rate = Balls bowled ÷ Wickets taken — the average number of balls per wicket.

• "Batting rate" is not a recognised cricketing term.

NOTE

• Cricket's governing body is the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered in Dubai, UAE. In India the game is governed by the BCCI (founded 1928).

question: Yuki Bhambri and Saketh Myneni won the Bangkok Open Challenger title 2023. They are related to which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Yuki Bhambri and Saketh Myneni are Indian tennis players. In 2023 the pair won the men's doubles title at the Bangkok Open Challenger (an ATP Challenger Tour event). (टेनिस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Yuki Bhambri won the junior Australian Open boys' singles title in 2009 and was once the junior world No. 1.

• Saketh Myneni has represented India in the Davis Cup and won a gold medal in mixed doubles at the 2014 Asian Games (with Sania Mirza).

• The ATP Challenger Tour is the second tier of men's professional tennis, below the main ATP Tour.

NOTE

• Tennis's four Grand Slams: Australian Open (hard), French Open/Roland Garros (clay), Wimbledon (grass) and the US Open (hard).

• Other leading Indian tennis players: Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Rohan Bopanna, Sania Mirza and Sumit Nagal.

question: Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das and Gangadhar Pradhan are associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das and Gangadhar Pradhan are all celebrated gurus of the classical dance form "Odissi" of Odisha. (ओडिसी — ओडिशा)

• Along with Kelucharan Mohapatra, they were instrumental in reviving and codifying Odissi in the 20th century; the major gharanas of Odissi are named after these gurus.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Odissi is derived from the temple dance of the Maharis (temple dancers) and the Gotipuas (boy dancers) of Odisha, and finds sculptural evidence in the Udayagiri caves and the Konark Sun Temple.

• Its two basic postures are the Tribhanga (three bends of the body) and the Chauka (square stance representing Lord Jagannath).

• Odissi is often performed to the Gita Govinda of Jayadeva.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty listed in the Indian Constitution?
option_1: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
option_2: To engage in political activities to promote democracy
option_3: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
option_4: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
solution_text:
The correct answer is To engage in political activities to promote democracy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To engage in political activities to promote democracy" is NOT one of the Fundamental Duties. It does not appear anywhere in Article 51A of the Constitution. (यह मौलिक कर्तव्य नहीं है)

• The other three options are genuine Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A:

◦ 51A(c) — to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

◦ 51A(f) — to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.

◦ 51A(i) — to safeguard public property and to abjure violence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are contained in Part IV-A, Article 51A.

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 11th duty (a parent/guardian to provide education to a child aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts.

NOTE

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia). India is the only major democracy that lists such duties alongside fundamental rights.

question: As of 2022, 12-feet statue of Adi Shankaracharya, which was unveiled by the Prime Minister of India is located in _________
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kedarnath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A 12-feet-tall statue of Adi Shankaracharya was unveiled by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Kedarnath (Uttarakhand) on 5 November 2021, at the site of the saint's samadhi. (केदारनाथ — आदि शंकराचार्य की प्रतिमा)

• The statue, carved from chlorite schist stone, was installed as part of the Kedarnath reconstruction/redevelopment project following the 2013 floods.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Adi Shankaracharya (c. 788–820 CE), born at Kaladi in Kerala, was the great philosopher who propounded Advaita Vedanta (non-dualism).

• He established four mathas (monasteries) in the four corners of India: Sringeri (South, Karnataka), Dwarka (West, Gujarat), Puri (East, Odisha) and Jyotirmath/Badrinath (North, Uttarakhand).

NOTE

• Kedarnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and one of the Char Dham of Uttarakhand (Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath). It lies near the Mandakini river in the Garhwal Himalayas.

question: During cell division, the formation of a new cell wall is followed by the accumulation of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is phragmoplast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In plant cell division (cytokinesis), the formation of a new cell wall begins with the accumulation of a barrel-shaped structure of microtubules, microfilaments and vesicles called the "phragmoplast". (फ्रैग्मोप्लास्ट)

• The phragmoplast guides Golgi-derived vesicles to the centre of the dividing cell, where they fuse to form the cell plate, which grows outward and matures into the new cell wall.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Peristome" — the fringe of teeth around the opening of a moss capsule (also the rim of a shell/pitcher plant).

• "Periplasm" — the space between the inner and outer membranes of Gram-negative bacteria.

• "Protoplast" — a plant, bacterial or fungal cell whose cell wall has been completely removed.

NOTE

• Cytokinesis differs in the two kingdoms: animal cells divide by a cleavage furrow (constriction of the plasma membrane), while plant cells divide by the formation of a cell plate (because of their rigid cell wall).

question: Bhanu Ji is associated with which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhanu Ji (Bhanuji) is regarded as the founder of the Jaipur Gharana of Kathak. He was a temple dancer of Vrindavan whose descendants developed this style under the patronage of the Kachhwaha Rajput rulers of Jaipur. (जयपुर घराना — कथक)

• The Jaipur Gharana is known for its emphasis on layakari (rhythmic intricacy), fast footwork, pirouettes (chakkars) and technical virtuosity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak gharanas: Jaipur (founded by Bhanuji — emphasis on rhythm and footwork), Lucknow (founded by Ishwari Prasad; developed by Thakur Prasad and Bindadin Maharaj — emphasis on bhava/abhinaya, grace and expression), Banaras (founded by Janakiprasad) and Raigarh (developed under Raja Chakradhar Singh of Chhattisgarh).

• Famous Kathak exponents: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj and Gopi Krishna.

NOTE

• The word "Kathak" comes from "Katha" (story) — the kathakars were storytellers who narrated epics through dance. It is the only classical dance of India with a strong Persian/Mughal court influence.

question: Which of the following is an example of capital expenditure in the government budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Purchase of military equipment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Capital expenditure is expenditure that either creates assets for the government or reduces its liabilities. The "purchase of military equipment" creates a durable physical asset, so it is capital expenditure. (पूँजीगत व्यय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other three options are revenue expenditure — recurring expenses that neither create assets nor reduce liabilities:

◦ Interest payment on a loan — a recurring payment, does not reduce the principal liability.

◦ Maintenance of government buildings — upkeep, not creation of a new asset.

◦ Subsidies provided to farmers — a transfer payment.

• Other examples of capital expenditure: construction of roads, bridges, schools, hospitals, purchase of machinery, repayment of loans and loans given to states/PSUs.

NOTE

• Budget terminology: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts; Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings); Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement".

question: FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2023 was held in which Indian state/UT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2023 (the 15th edition) was hosted by India in Odisha, at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar and the newly built Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium, Rourkela (January 13–29, 2023). (ओडिशा)

• Germany won the title, beating Belgium in the final via a penalty shoot-out.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium in Rourkela is the largest hockey stadium in the world by seating capacity (about 21,800).

• Odisha also hosted the 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup at Bhubaneswar, which Belgium won.

• The state government of Odisha has been the principal sponsor of the Indian hockey teams since 2018.

NOTE

• Hockey is governed globally by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland. India won the men's hockey World Cup in 1975 (Kuala Lumpur) — its only title so far.

question: An image of which of the following elements is shown by the map of Cyprus from which the element got its name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Copper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The element "Copper" derives its name from the island of Cyprus. The Romans called it "cyprium aes" ("metal of Cyprus"), which was later shortened to "cuprum" — hence the English "copper" and the chemical symbol "Cu". (ताँबा — साइप्रस से नाम)

• Cyprus was the main source of copper for the ancient Mediterranean world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Copper (Cu): atomic number 29, a reddish-brown, highly ductile metal and an excellent conductor of electricity and heat, hence widely used in electrical wiring.

• Alloys: Brass = copper + zinc; Bronze = copper + tin.

• In India, the main copper-producing states are Rajasthan (Khetri), Madhya Pradesh (Malanjkhand) and Jharkhand (Singhbhum).

NOTE

• Other elements named after places: Polonium (Poland), Francium (France), Germanium (Germany), Americium (America), Ruthenium (Russia), Scandium (Scandinavia).

question:
Consider the following statements about Abhinav Bharat Society.

1) The society was a community of socialists believed in an armed revolution.

2) The society was founded by Jaya Prakash Narayan.

3) Mitra Mela, a revolutionary secret society was renamed Abhinav Bharat in 1904.

Select the correct statement(s) using the codes given below.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is correct — the Abhinav Bharat Society was a secret revolutionary organisation whose members believed in achieving independence through armed revolution.

• Statement 2 is incorrect — it was NOT founded by Jaya Prakash Narayan. It was founded by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (Veer Savarkar) along with his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar.

• Statement 3 is correct — the society originally began as "Mitra Mela" (founded in 1899 at Nasik) and was renamed "Abhinav Bharat" in 1904.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The name "Abhinav Bharat" ("Young India") was inspired by Giuseppe Mazzini's "Young Italy" movement.

• The society had branches in India and abroad (London) and was linked to the Nasik Conspiracy Case (1909), in which Anant Laxman Kanhere shot the Collector A. M. T. Jackson.

• It was formally dissolved in 1952.

NOTE

• Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) was a socialist leader associated with the Congress Socialist Party (1934), the Quit India Movement and later the Total Revolution (Sampoorna Kranti) movement of the 1970s; he was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously.

question: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA) was launched in the year 2020 by which Ministry of Government of India?
option_1: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
option_2: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
option_3: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Rural Development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA)" was launched on 20 June 2020 from Telihar village, Khagaria district, Bihar, and is coordinated by the Ministry of Rural Development. (ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय)

• It was a ₹50,000 crore employment-cum-rural public works campaign of 125 days aimed at providing livelihood opportunities to migrant workers who returned to their villages during the COVID-19 lockdown.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Abhiyaan covered 116 districts across 6 states — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and Odisha — each having received a large number of returning migrants.

• It involved the convergence of 12 different ministries/departments and focused on 25 categories of works (village roads, Anganwadi centres, water conservation, laying of optical fibre, etc.).

NOTE

• Other schemes of the Ministry of Rural Development: MGNREGA, PMAY-Gramin, DAY-NRLM, DDU-GKY, PMGSY and the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).

question: Who among the following is the author of the Hindi novel ‘Raag Darbari’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shrilal Shukla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Raag Darbari" (1968) is the celebrated Hindi satirical novel written by Shrilal Shukla. (श्रीलाल शुक्ल — रागदरबारी)

• It won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1969 and is a biting satire on the decay of values in post-independence rural North India, set in the fictional village of Shivpalganj.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Shrilal Shukla was awarded the Jnanpith Award (2009) and the Padma Bhushan (2008).

• Rahul Sankrityayan — called the "Father of Hindi travel literature"; works include "Volga Se Ganga" and "Meri Jeevan Yatra".

• Premchand (Dhanpat Rai Srivastava) — "Godaan", "Gaban", "Nirmala", "Karmabhoomi"; known as the "Upanyas Samrat".

• Kashinath Singh — "Kashi Ka Assi", "Apna Morcha".

NOTE

• "Raag Darbari" has been adapted for television and translated into many languages; the English translation by Gillian Wright won the Sahitya Akademi translation prize.

question: Who is the first female classical dancer in Indian history to be nominated as a Member of Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Parliament of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904–1986) was the first woman classical dancer (Bharatanatyam) to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha — she was nominated in 1952. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल)

• She was a pioneering Bharatanatyam revivalist who restored the dance from the sadir tradition and gave it social respectability.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• She founded "Kalakshetra" at Adyar, Chennai (1936), a renowned institution for classical dance and music, now an Institution of National Importance.

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1956) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, and famously declined the offer of the office of the President of India in 1977.

• Sanjukta Panigrahi was a celebrated Odissi dancer; Shobha Naidu was a leading Kuchipudi exponent.

NOTE

• Under Article 80 of the Constitution, the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from persons with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

question: What does the term ‘Overdraft’ mean in banking?
option_1: The process of transferring funds between bank accounts
option_2: The maximum withdrawal limit from an ATM
solution_text:
The correct answer is Short-term financing facility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Overdraft (OD)" is a short-term financing/credit facility by which a bank allows an account holder to withdraw more money than the balance available in the account, up to a sanctioned limit. (ओवरड्राफ्ट — अल्पकालिक ऋण सुविधा)

• Interest is charged only on the amount actually overdrawn and for the period it is used.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Overdraft facilities are usually extended on current accounts of businesses, and also against security such as fixed deposits, salary, shares, insurance policies or property.

• Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), an overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000 is available to eligible account holders.

• A related facility is the Cash Credit (CC) account, granted against the hypothecation of stock/inventory.

NOTE

• Other banking terms: Repo Rate (rate at which RBI lends to banks), Reverse Repo Rate, CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio), SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) and NPA (Non-Performing Asset).

question: Which of the following is an example of Eastern Ghats peak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahendragiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mahendragiri" (about 1,501 m) in the Gajapati district of Odisha is a well-known peak of the Eastern Ghats. (महेंद्रगिरि — पूर्वी घाट)

• The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous, eroded chain of hills running along India's eastern coast, cut through by the rivers Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Doddabetta (2,637 m) — the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills, Tamil Nadu (Western Ghats).

• Anamudi (2,695 m) — the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India, in Kerala.

• Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) — the highest peak of the Aravalli Range, at Mount Abu, Rajasthan.

• Arma Konda / Jindhagada peak (1,680 m) in Andhra Pradesh is generally regarded as the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats.

NOTE

• The Western Ghats are continuous, higher and receive heavy orographic rainfall; they are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world's biodiversity hotspots. The Nilgiris form the junction of the Western and Eastern Ghats.

question: Indian musician, Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia used to play which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia (born 1938, Allahabad) is India's most celebrated exponent of the bansuri (bamboo flute), a wind instrument. (बाँसुरी वादक)

• He was trained by Annapurna Devi, daughter of Baba Allauddin Khan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (2000), the Padma Bhushan (1992) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• With santoor maestro Pandit Shivkumar Sharma he formed the duo "Shiv-Hari", composing music for films such as Silsila, Chandni, Lamhe and Darr.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tat/Chordophones (string — sitar, sarod, veena, violin), Sushir/Aerophones (wind — bansuri, shehnai), Avanaddha/Membranophones (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj) and Ghan/Idiophones (solid — manjira, ghatam).

• Other maestros: Ravi Shankar (sitar), Amjad Ali Khan (sarod), Bismillah Khan (shehnai), Zakir Hussain (tabla), Shivkumar Sharma (santoor).

question: Which of the following was the first major and decisive victory for the East India Company on the soil of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Battle of Plassey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Battle of Plassey", fought on 23 June 1757, was the first major and decisive victory of the English East India Company in India. (प्लासी का युद्ध, 1757)

• It was fought between Robert Clive (East India Company) and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, on the banks of the Bhagirathi river near Palashi (Murshidabad, West Bengal).

• The Nawab was betrayed by his commander Mir Jafar, along with Rai Durlabh, Jagat Seth and Omichund; Mir Jafar was then installed as the puppet Nawab of Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Plassey marked the beginning of British political rule in India and gave the Company enormous financial resources from Bengal.

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) — Company (Hector Munro) vs the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II — confirmed British supremacy and led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), granting the Company the Diwani (revenue rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

NOTE

• The First Anglo-Maratha War (1775–82) ended with the Treaty of Salbai; the Battle of Tiruvannamalai (1767) was fought during the First Anglo-Mysore War; the Battle of Sindhuli (1767) was a Nepali (Gorkha) victory over the Company.

question: Which of the following locations receives the most rainfall in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mawsynram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mawsynram", in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, receives the highest average annual rainfall in India (and in the world) — roughly 11,872 mm. (मॉसिनराम — सर्वाधिक वर्षा)

• The heavy rainfall is caused by the funnelling of the moisture-laden Bay of Bengal branch of the south-west monsoon against the steep Khasi Hills, producing intense orographic rainfall.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Cherrapunji (Sohra), about 15 km away, is the second wettest place and holds the record for the highest rainfall in a single year and single month.

• Jaisalmer (Rajasthan) lies in the Thar Desert and is among the driest places in India (about 150–200 mm).

• Prayagraj and Guwahati receive moderate to high but far lower rainfall than Mawsynram.

NOTE

• The south-west monsoon (June–September) brings about 75% of India's annual rainfall through its two branches — the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch. The rain-shadow area east of the Western Ghats receives very little rain.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the literacy rate recorded in Kerala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 94.0%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Kerala recorded a literacy rate of about 94%, the highest among all Indian states. (केरल — 94% साक्षरता)

• Kerala's male literacy was about 96.1% and female literacy about 92.1%, the smallest gender gap in the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• All-India literacy rate (2011): 74.04% — male 82.14%, female 65.46%.

• Highest literacy among states: Kerala (94%) > Lakshadweep (91.8%, UT) > Mizoram (91.3%) > Goa (88.7%) > Tripura.

• Lowest literacy: Bihar (61.8%), followed by Arunachal Pradesh and Rajasthan.

• Most populous state: Uttar Pradesh; least populous: Sikkim.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years; the 2011 Census was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence. Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future". A literate person is one aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.

question: The Digital Lok Adalat, powered by AI (Artificial Intelligence) and Blockchain, was launched by the then National Legal Services Authority Chairman ___________ during the 18th All India Legal Services Authorities’ meet held in Jaipur in July 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice Uday Umesh Lalit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Digital Lok Adalat", powered by Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain, was launched in July 2022 at Jaipur during the 18th All India Legal Services Authorities' Meet by the then Executive Chairman of NALSA, Justice Uday Umesh Lalit. (न्यायमूर्ति यू. यू. ललित)

• Justice U. U. Lalit later became the 49th Chief Justice of India (August–November 2022).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) was constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (which came into force in 1995) to provide free legal aid to weaker sections and to organise Lok Adalats.

• The Chief Justice of India is the Patron-in-Chief of NALSA, and the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is its Executive Chairman.

• Article 39A (a Directive Principle, inserted by the 42nd Amendment) provides for equal justice and free legal aid.

NOTE

• A Lok Adalat ("People's Court") settles disputes by compromise/conciliation; its award is deemed a decree of a civil court and is final and binding, with no appeal allowed.

question: Janmashtami is a Hindu festival that celebrates the birth (janma) of the god, Krishna on the eighth (ashtami) day of the dark fortnight of the Hindu month of _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhadrapada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Krishna Janmashtami is celebrated on the eighth day (Ashtami) of the dark fortnight (Krishna Paksha) of the Hindu month of "Bhadrapada" (August–September). (भाद्रपद कृष्ण पक्ष अष्टमी)

• In the Purnimanta calendar followed in North India the same day falls in Shravana, but by the Amanta reckoning (used in Maharashtra, Gujarat and the South) it falls in Bhadrapada, which is the answer given here.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The festival marks the birth of Lord Krishna, the eighth avatar of Vishnu, at Mathura. It is celebrated with fasting, midnight puja, jhankis, Rasleela and the Dahi Handi (Govinda) event in Maharashtra.

• Major centres of celebration: Mathura, Vrindavan, Dwarka, Puri, Nathdwara and Udupi.

NOTE

• The twelve months of the Hindu calendar: Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashwin, Kartik, Margashirsha, Pausha, Magha, Phalguna.

• Other festivals of Bhadrapada: Ganesh Chaturthi, Hartalika Teej and Onam.

question: Which of the following music directors is known as ‘Mozart of Madras’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AR Rahman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A. R. Rahman (born A. S. Dileep Kumar in 1967 at Madras/Chennai) is popularly known as the "Mozart of Madras" — a title given by Time magazine for his prolific and innovative compositions. (मद्रास का मोत्ज़ार्ट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He won two Academy Awards (Oscars), two Grammy Awards, a Golden Globe and a BAFTA for the music of "Slumdog Millionaire" (2008) — including "Jai Ho".

• He has received the Padma Bhushan (2010), Padma Shri (2000) and six National Film Awards. His debut film as a composer was "Roja" (1992).

• He also composed "Vande Mataram" (1997) and "Maa Tujhe Salaam".

NOTE

question: What is the tenure of the Vice-President of India?
option_2: Until he wants to hold the office
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vice-President of India holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office. (उपराष्ट्रपति का कार्यकाल — 5 वर्ष)

• However, he may continue in office beyond five years until his successor assumes charge, and he is eligible for re-election any number of times.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Vice-President is elected under Article 66 by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament (elected and nominated) through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote and secret ballot.

• Qualifications (Article 66): citizen of India, at least 35 years of age, qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha, and not holding an office of profit.

• He is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64) and acts as President in case of a vacancy (Article 65).

NOTE

• He may resign by writing to the President and can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha (14 days' notice required). Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was India's first Vice-President.
